domain: EU/EEA environmental regulation - urban waste water treatment plant (UWWTP) reported performance across the biennial UWWTD Article 15 reporting cycles (EU agency publisher, 30 EEA countries reporting)
prediction_question: For an urban waste water treatment plant active in UWWTD reporting cycle N, will that plant be reported as FAILING at least one treatment-performance parameter (any of uwwBOD5Perf, uwwCODPerf, uwwNTotPerf, uwwPTotPerf, uwwTSSPerf, uwwOtherPerf = 'F') in the next reporting cycle, given only features documented and reported in cycles up to and including N: country/NUTS, organic design capacity (uwwCapacity, p.e.), load entering the plant (uwwLoadEnteringUWWTP), mean annual volume treated (uwwWasteWaterTreated), treatment train flags (primary/secondary/more-stringent/N-removal/P-removal/microfiltration/UV/ozonation...), plant age from uwwBeginLife, and the plant's own performance flags reported in cycles <= N?
prediction_time: The publication instant of reporting cycle N (a statistical release): all feature cycles are <= N and the target is the performance assessment published in cycle N+1. Measured anchors: the 13th data call (situation at 2022-12-31 per ReportPeriod.csv) was published as FINAL PUBLIC VERSION in Oct 2025 per the catalogue record; the per-country delivery versions (repVersion) for that call are dated 2023-12 to 2025-04 (e.g. SI 2025-04-24, most MS 2024-06). Cycle cadence is biennial (Directive 91/271/EEC Art. 15, reported on the Commission's request), so the lead time is roughly two reporting cycles. The exact publication dates of the older cycles are to be pinned at construction from their catalogue records; the per-country repSituationAt/repVersion fields are already documented in the source (ReportPeriod.csv) and ship with the data.
target_definition: Binary from the source row of cycle N+1: label = 1 iff the plant (uwwState=1, active) has at least one treatment-performance parameter assessed 'F' among the six uww*Perf fields, restricted to plants with at least one answered (P or F) parameter; plants with only NA/NR/blank assessments are unobserved-target rows, counted separately, never dropped silently. Measured on the full 2023 call CSV: 2,411 positives / 21,537 answered (11.2% base rate). The uww*Perf codes are P/F/NA/NR (documented in the Eionet data dictionary element pages, e.g. element 104947 'Treatment performance: BOD5'); the 'In cause of failure' fields (uwwBadPerformance 'Bad performance' 1,765 Yes among active, uwwBadDesign 'Bad design or dimensioning', uwwAccidents 'Major accidents', uwwInformation free text) describe the reported CAUSE where the plant does not meet requirements and are label-source/label-adjacent columns, excluded from features. IMPORTANT measured property recorded as part of the definition: the label is 'REPORTED as failing' - a mixture of physical performance and the national reporting regime; measured 2023-call any-F rates range from DE 0.4% (16/3,776) and BE 2.8% to NO 49.6% (116/234), HR 53.5% (46/86) and RO 36.3% (352/971). Country is therefore a legitimate feature AND the reference baseline must be country-stratified; the mixture is the task's documented semantics, not a defect to hide.

construction_script: planned: candidates/eea-uwwtd-plant-poor-performance/source/build.py (stdlib only; download the public cycle zips, normalise the per-cycle UWWTPS tables, join plants across cycles on uwwCode (join measured at construction), emit one row per (plant, cycle transition) with features from cycles <= N and the any-F label from cycle N+1; unobserved targets counted; runner layout + qualification gate on a worker)
split_strategy: Temporal by reporting cycle: train on early-cycle transitions, eval on middle cycles, holdout on the newest public cycles (2021-2022 provisional / 2022-2023 final at the far end). Both classes are present in every measured cycle window (2023 call: 11.2% positives, 21,537 answered plants, 30 reporters). MEASURED CAVEAT: only the 2022-2023 cycle was downloaded and measured this session (2,411 positives); the 2011-2012, 2021-2022 and any recoverable 2007-2020 cycles are confirmed public only by catalogue/share-link HEAD probes, not by row counts - construction step 1 is to pin the public cycle inventory and measure the uwwCode join rate between at least two cycles. Positives cluster by country reporting regime (measured: any-F rate DE 0.4% vs NO 49.6%), so clustered/stratified counts per split must be reported; a split that puts a country's plants only in train and only in eval would measure regime shift, not plant performance.

prior_art: Process-level WWTP effluent-ML literature (sensor/time-series); JRC European WWTP database (descriptive, 2015 vintage); EEA UWWTD viewer and Commission implementation reports (aggregate compliance statistics).
novelty_check.theirs: The EEA publishes the raw per-cycle Waterbase tables and spatial GeoPackages, compliance statistics in Commission UWWTD implementation reports, and an interactive viewer; process-control ML literature predicts effluent quality from plant sensor time series (a different formulation, different data); the JRC maintains a descriptive European WWTP infrastructure database. No public prediction task with splits and a scored contract exists on this source.
novelty_check.ours: Per-plant, per-reporting-cycle panel built from the EEA's published UWWTD Waterbase cycles (2007-2023 biennial Art.15 reporting, ~24k active plants x 30 reporters): predict whether an active urban wastewater treatment plant will be reported as failing at least one treatment-performance parameter (uwwBOD5Perf..uwwOtherPerf = F) in the NEXT reporting cycle, from features documented in the Eionet data dictionary and reported in earlier cycles (capacity, load, treatment train, NUTS, country, age, previous-cycle flags). Temporal cross-cycle splits, a scored binary contract, and the national reporting-mixture property measured and documented.
novelty_check.rule: A dataset that already exists in ML-ready form is not published. Mirroring is a failure mode, not a contribution.

jurisdiction.publisher: European Environment Agency (EEA), an EU agency headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark; the data are Member State and EEA-country deliveries under Directive 91/271/EEC (Urban Waste Water Treatment Directive) Article 15, validated and published by the EEA
jurisdiction.convention: Supranational EU agency; 'EU' recorded as the country because an agency of the Union has the Union's jurisdiction, per the same convention as ecdc-atlas-surveillance and eutl-installation-net-short. The reporting population includes EEA non-EU countries (CH, NO, IS) - the publisher's jurisdiction is the EU.
